newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Tietmeyer warns markets against hopes on US rates.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer warns markets against hopes on US rates.

text.p: BASLE, Switzerland, April 7 (Reuter) Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer on Monday said markets should be cautious in expecting further U.S. interest rate changes after the U.S. Federal Reserve ended its 20-month easing period on March 25.

"Of course we have to look at how markets will react, but one should be very cautious in expecting that this is the beginning of further moves, but of course it is all up to authorities in the U.S.," Tietmeyer said.
The Fed nudged its short-term fed funds rate up by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent, the first interest rate hike in over two years.

Tietmeyer, in Basle for the monthly Group of 10 (G-10) central bank governors meeting, said the G-10 had discussed the recent U.S. interest rate rise and what motivated this decision and the rationale behind it.
The governors had had a short exchange on the market reaction and the implications for further monetary policy in the U.S., Tietmeyer said.
But Tietmeyer also said that conditions were now different than they were in 1994, when the bond markets were sent into a tailspin.
"All in all we see the situation as different from for example 1994 because capital market rates are more on solid ground and we don't see any excessive developments."
The U.S. was represented by Fed Governor Lawrence Meyer, who was attending the meeting in Basle for the first time.
